whole.note: The whole-body sheet of the same character, with the same framing (frame size, scale and feet pivot) as the legs and torso sheets, so a game can swap between it and the composited pair at the same ground point: the whole sheet for moves without mouse aim (keyboard play, prone, death…), the legs + torso pair while aiming apart from the walk.

split.note: Two sheets of one character with one framing. Each frame of both has a `waist` socket (untrimmed-frame pixels; flipX: x = frameWidth - x). Draw the legs frame for the walk direction at the character's ground point (the usual pivot), then the torso frame for the aim direction on top, placed so its waist socket lands on the legs frame's waist socket: torso.x = legs.x + legsWaist.x - torsoWaist.x (same for y), in untrimmed-frame pixels. The torso always draws over the legs. A clip on both sheets (idle, crouch, death…) drawn in one direction is the whole body again.
